metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Placed on IR
metadata.description: Hudson (pectoral) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end this season.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Expected to miss rest of season
metadata.description: Hudson's agent revealed Tuesday that the tight end sustained a torn pectoral in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins and is expected to miss the rest of the season, Charlie Clifford of WLWT News 5 Cincinnati reports.
metadata.analysis: Hudson will presumably need surgery to address the pec tear and is likely to be placed on injured reserve in the coming days. Though he didn't win a spot on the Bengals' initial 53-man roster coming out of the preseason, Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the team's firs three games before getting signed to the roster Sept. 29. Over his four appearances with Cincinnati, the reserve tight end tallied seven catches for 33 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson (pectoral) to miss rest of the season
metadata.description: Tanner Hudson (pectoral) will miss the rest of the season.
metadata.analysis: After hauling in his first touchdown pass of the campaign in Week 5, Hudson is dealing with a torn pectoral that will force him out for the remainder of the season. Erick All Jr. saw an uptick in snaps after Hudson left Sunday's game.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson Expected to Miss Entire Season With Torn Pec
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson (pectoral) suffered a torn pectoral muscle in the Week 5 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday and is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, his agent told WLWT's Charlie Clifford. Hudson only had seven receptions for 33 yards and one touchdown in four games played this year with the Bengals, but it is a big loss in the team's TE corps behind starter Mike Gesicki. The good news for the Bengals is that they have a deep group of tight ends behind Gesicki, which also includes Drew Sample and Erick All Jr. Hudson had the best season of his career in 2023 in his first year with the Bengals, catching 39 of his 50 targets for 352 yards and one touchdown in 12 games played. He has never scored more than two touchdowns in any of his eight seasons in the league, but he is a well-respected pass-catching backup TE when he is healthy.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Dealing with pec injury
metadata.description: Hudson suffered a pectoral injury during the Bengals' 31-24 win over the Dolphins on Sunday, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Hudson finished Sunday's game having caught all three of his targets for 14 yards, which included a two-yard touchdown grab late in the second quarter to give the Bengals a 21-7 halftime lead. He played a total of 27 snaps (19 on offense, eight on special teams), and although it's unclear when he picked up the injury, it's severe enough to potentially require a stint on injured reserve. Rookie seventh-rounder Jack Endries would be in line for a larger role if Hudson misses time.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson hauls in touchdown Sunday
metadata.description: Tanner Hudson hauled in three passes for 14 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins.
metadata.analysis: Hudson was able to contribute well on Sunday. He caught three passes on the day, and while that only turned into 14 yards, he was able to get into the end zone for a touchdown on one of those catches. He is not expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Signed to Cincinnati's active roster
metadata.description: The Bengals signed Hudson off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the Bengals' first three games of the regular season, accumulating three catches on as many targets for 17 yards. He'll now be a part of the team's 53-man roster moving forward and will contribute mostly on special teams and in a depth role on offense behind fellow tight ends Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson signs with Bengals' active roster
metadata.description: The Bengals signed TE Tanner Hudson to their active roster.
metadata.analysis: Hudson will add depth in the tight end room for Cincinnati.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Back to practice squad
metadata.description: Hudson reverted to the Bengals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Hudson caught both of his targets for 13 yards in Sunday's loss to the Steelers. The 31-year-old tight end has appeared in two games this season, securing all three of his targets for 17 yards. The Bengals like to use multiple tight ends, and Hudson played behind both Drew Sample and Mike Gesicki but ahead of Erick All against Pittsburgh. Hudson would likely need an injury to Gesicki to become relevant in fantasy.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Elevated for Sunday's showdown
metadata.description: The Bengals elevated Hudson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Hudson was elevated for the Bengals' Week 1 win over the Buccaneers, playing six offensive snaps and 13 special-teams snaps in the contest and catching his sole target for four yards. The tight end should fill a similar role in Sunday's game against the Steelers, providing special teams coverage alongside a minimal offensive snap share.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Moves back to practice squad
metadata.description: Hudson reverted to the Bengals' practice squad after catching one pass for four yards in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Bucs, per the NFL's official transaction log.
metadata.analysis: The tight end played on six offensive snaps and 13 special-teams snaps. Hudson got the nod over rookie seventh-round pick Jack Endries as the fourth tight end on Cincinnati's depth chart. Endries, though, is not injured, so it's not clear which player will hold down the spot if the Bengals again carry four players at the position in their next game.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Elevated for Sunday
metadata.description: The Bengals elevated Hudson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
metadata.analysis: Hudson was released by the Bengals in late August before returning to the team on the practice squad. The tight end was unable to make the original 53-man roster over Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All or Jack Endries, but it appears the team would like him to suit up for Sunday's game alongside the other four options anyway.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Returns to Cincinnati
metadata.description: The Bengals signed Hudson to the practice squad Tuesday.
metadata.analysis: While Hudson was unable to make the Bengals' initial 53-man roster, the organization still wants the tight end around. If Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All or Jack Endries must miss time due to injury, Hudson will likely be elevated from the practice squad to the active roster to fill the open role.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson released by Bengals
metadata.description: The Bengals released TE Tanner Hudson.
metadata.analysis: Hudson will figure to seek another opportunity heading into the season.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Let go by Cincinnati
metadata.description: The Bengals released Hudson on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Hudson signed a one-year contract extension with the Bengals in January. The tight end played in 15 regular-season games for the team during 2025, producing 19 receptions for 168 yards and two touchdowns. The Bengals ultimately ended up keeping Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample, Erick All and Jack Endries at tight end. Hudson is now a free agent and can sign with any franchise's 53-man roster or practice squad.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson signs one-year extension with Bengals
metadata.description: Tanner Hudson has agreed to a one-year contract extension to remain with the Cincinnati Bengals.
metadata.analysis: Hudson played a career-high 15 games with the Bengals last season, but was limited to just 148 offensive snaps. He managed to catch 19 passes for 168 yards and two touchdowns. The tight end's best season came in 2023 when he hauled in 39 catches for 352 yards. If Noah Fant leaves via free agency, Hudson could see some more opportunities in 2026.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Inks contract extension
metadata.description: Hudson and the Bengals agreed to a one-year contract extension Monday.
metadata.analysis: Hudson played in 15 games for Cincinnati during the 2025 campaign, posting a 19-168-2 receiving line that was a near carbon copy of his 19-154-1 line from 2024, though he saw action in just 11 regular-season contests during that 2024 campaign. His past two seasons have paled in comparison to his 2023 campaign when he recorded 39 catches on 50 targets for 352 yards a touchdown across 12 regular-season games, but the Bengals value his contributions enough to keep in the fold for at least another season. Mike Gesicki will likely remain Cincinnati's No. 1 tight end next year, but Hudson could fill a bigger role if Noah Fant, who is slated to be a free agent, doesn't return.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Another 19-catch season
metadata.description: Hudson finished the 2025 regular season with 19 catches for 168 yards and two touchdowns on 24 targets.
metadata.analysis: Hudson recorded exactly 19 catches for a second consecutive season while setting career highs in both games played (15) and touchdowns (two). The seven-year NFL veteran will be an unrestricted free agent this offseason after spending the last three seasons in Cincinnati.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Season-high three grabs in Week 15
metadata.description: Hudson recorded three catches for 16 yards on five targets in Sunday's 24-0 loss to the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: The three receptions were one shy of matching a season-high total for Hudson, who took the field for 19 of the team's 43 offensive snaps. Though Hudson has demonstrated some solid pass-catching chops when he's on the field, he's still no better than the second or third receiving option at the position behind Mike Gesicki and Noah Fant, the latter of whom exited Sunday with an ankle injury. The Bengals also continue to keep Drew Sample involved on offense as a blocking specialist, which typically leaves few snaps left over for Hudson.

metadata.title: Tanner Hudson - Catches highlight-reel touchdown
metadata.description: Hudson had just one catch for 14 yards in Thursday night's win over the Ravens, but it was a spectacular one-handed grab in the corner of the end zone to help the Bengals stretch their lead to two scores.
metadata.analysis: Joe Burrow led Hudson perfectly to the corner, after Hudson had beaten the Ravens' Kyle Hamilton. Amazingly, Hudson played just six offensive snaps in the game as the Bengals' third tight end, with Mike Gesicki back in the rotation.
